label: Florida Restores Felons' Voting Rights
detail: Florida lets people with past felony convictions vote in the 2000 presidential election.
assumption: Floridians barred by a felony conviction (Sentencing Project estimates by race [I]) become eligible and vote like the rest of their census group in Florida. Studies (Uggen & Manza 2002) estimate they would have turned out less but leaned strongly toward the administration party.
facts_text: Florida has ended its lifetime ban on voting for people with felony convictions, and those who have completed their sentences are registered to vote in the November election.
Election officials estimate that several hundred thousand Floridians are newly eligible.
research_questions: How many Floridians were barred from voting in 2000 because of felony convictions, and what was their racial makeup?
How much do ex-offenders turn out compared with other voters of similar age and background?
How have people with felony records voted when rights were restored, in Florida or elsewhere?
borrowed: US-born Black and US-born non-Hispanic white men in the south
source_text: Florida restores voting rights to people with felony convictions before the 2000 election.
hand_edited: reach narrowed to Florida and the action limited to the felony bar (the compiled spec enfranchised every Southern adult; DISCLOSURES).
